A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Kendall-based logit-distillation work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and object-detection experiments using RKKD, including CIFAR-100, ImageNet, COCO2017, transformer students, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds loss-component controls, diagnostic analyses, DIST combinations, and further ImageNet results.

M1.justification: The auxiliary Kendall/tanh loss, KL and cross-entropy combination, normalization, and three variants remain. However, v2 corrects the written loss to sum over unique pairs j<i and consistently includes k in tanh and 2k in its exponential expansion (Equations 5–7). These are limited formulation corrections; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100 and ImageNet classification and COCO2017 object detection. Transformer students and detection already appear in v1 Section 5.2. The added ImageNet model pair and diagnostic experiments do not introduce a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds DIST and LSKD to the CIFAR-100 comparisons in Tables 1–2, CTKD to the COCO comparison in Table 5, and NKD to the ImageNet evaluation in Table 13. Table 12 additionally evaluates DIST with the proposed loss. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds the ResNet34-to-ResNet18 ImageNet configuration and loss-component and joint-weight controls. Table 1 drops the full ResNet32×4-to-SHN-V2 comparison, although this pair remains in ablations. Table 5 changes the reported metric from AP70 to AP75 while retaining shared values; this establishes a reporting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds gradient-versus-logit diagnostics, ranking-only versus KL-only controls, training curves, ranking-alignment visualizations, joint-coefficient sensitivity, LSKD probability analysis, and DIST-combination experiments. These investigate optimization mechanisms and complementary information beyond v1's analyses. The three-form, temperature, normalization, and top/min-channel analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates and some averages across architectures; the added results do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result blocks, including ranking-only controls, DIST combinations, and further ImageNet comparisons. Table 12 reports 75.85 versus 75.58 for DIST with versus without ranking loss on ResNet32×4-to-WRN-16-2; Table 13 reports 72.06 versus 71.96 for NKD on ResNet34-to-ResNet18. Most matched original scores remain unchanged. Table 1 removes SHN-V2 comparison entries, and Table 5 corrects the AP gain from +21.86 to +1.86.

T1.justification: v2 substantially expands the mathematical analysis with explicit KL and ranking-loss gradient derivations in Section 4.2.1 and Appendix A.5. It also corrects pair indexing and the tanh expansion and documents the latter in Appendix A.6. The earlier optimal-solution-domain argument is retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a complementary ranking loss for logit distillation. v2 adds channel-scale robustness of ranking gradients as an explicit claim in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It foregrounds existing COCO and CNN/ViT applicability while deemphasizing the three loss variants in the contribution summary.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of early convergence, late-stage compatibility with KL, why cross-entropy may provide insufficient guidance, and complementarity with Pearson-based DIST. Appendix A.7 interprets LSKD's remaining low-probability channels. The explicit downstream-task limitation in v1 Appendix A.1 disappears despite unchanged task coverage.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link and Algorithm 1, which explicitly specifies mean/std normalization of logits for the ranking term. It also discloses COCO batch size 8 and dataset counts. Existing training details largely remain, but v1's explicit CIFAR-100 and ImageNet image resolutions are omitted. The linked code was not accessed.

R1.justification: Appendix A.8 newly positions Kendall ranking against DIST's Pearson correlation. References add DIST, NKD, COCO, and other works, while removing Kendall's original citation and several transformer architecture references. The overall related-work structure and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten, and RKKD terminology becomes generic ranking-loss terminology. The methodological discussion is reorganized into gradient, optimal-domain, and classification perspectives. Loss variants move to the appendix, temperature ablation moves into the main text, and the appendix is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout, redraws and relocates introductory figures, and adds gradient, training-curve, ranking-alignment, sensitivity, and probability-distribution displays. Tables gain comparison rows and revised highlighting, Table 1 loses a column, and an algorithm box is introduced. Existing analyses are also resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The ranking-only control, closer DIST/LSKD comparisons, and DIST-combination experiment improve the evidence for the loss's complementary value. Algorithm 1 also clarifies previously unspecified normalization. These address weaknesses in v1's comparative support and implementation documentation. The gain is tempered by problems in the expanded theory, including a factor-of-two mismatch between the ranking loss in Equation 32 and its stated gradient in Equation 37.
